acceptanceCriteria: An active task on one branch writes its planned src file while a parallel task on another branch claims it
core/bug-registry does not judge a finished fix task that only claims the staged history file
With no readable branch, the tasks whose records the scope touches are judged
diagnosis: Reproduced: in a consumer repo, task B in implementation on feature/active-b writes its planned src/widget.ts and is denied by core/workflow-gates and core/writes-within-plan on behalf of task A, a planning task on feature/parallel-a whose files.allow also claims src/**; at L3 a docs commit on a branch whose history entry has no Bug field is blocked by core/bug-registry because finished fix tasks T-0020..T-0022 claim docs/HISTORY. Root cause: scope-tasks.ts readJudgedTasks and collectTaskFindings add every task whose files.allow glob matches a scope file (tasksForScope), and records-guards.ts bugRegistryReal reads only those claiming tasks, assuming a claim means ownership of the change. SPEC 4.12.1 makes the branch's active task the task every hook judges and 4.12.3 L4 judges the tasks touched in the PR. Fix: the judged set is the active task plus each task whose record (.codictator/tasks/<id>.json) is in the judged scope; every task-judging helper and bugRegistryReal use it.
